messages:
morgan: heads up — seeing a small but growing spike of GPU pods stuck in Pending in eu-west1c. warm-pool slots seem to be hanging on lease handshake. Grafana: <https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/slots/gpu-warmpool?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west1c>

rao: how many pods stuck? any common nodeSelector/affinity? can you paste `kubectl get pods -o wide` for one of them?

morgan: ~18 pods pending across 6 nodes. example:
```
NAME                      READY   STATUS    NODE              AGE
train-copy-5-xyz          0/1     Pending   <none>            3m
```
and `kubectl describe pod train-copy-5-xyz` shows a repeated msg:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age    From               Message
  ----     ------            ----   ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m     default-scheduler  pod didn't match available volumes/affinity
  Normal   BindAttempt       1m     warmpool-controller  attempted lease handshake, timeout
```

taylor: last scheduler rollout changed lateBindRetry from 1 -> 3 two days ago. could be exposing NIC qdisc/backpressure. any node logs for `kubelet` or `device-plugin` around handshake time?

infra-bot: autoscaler: added 2 nodes to eu-west1c at 2024-11-03T10:12:04Z due to scale up. node pool: gpu-rt-eu-west1c-7

elena: i've been seeing `vfio`/driver reconnects on nodes with nvidia-driver 535.3 — kernel oops rate bumped after the driver update. filing HW-driver ticket LINK-1234, cc infra-hw.

jamal: short-term mitigation: 1) make warm-pool leases soft so latebind doesn't block scheduling; 2) increase warm-pool target by 25% to absorb handshake latency; 3) relax pod anti-affinity if possible.
Try patch:
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap/warmpool-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"leaseMode":"soft","targetSize":"125"}}'
```

morgan: applied the `leaseMode=soft` patch and bumped pool target. started seeing binds succeed after ~45s for queued pods. still seeing occasional NIC errs but scheduling resumed. cost note: warm-pool extra nodes ~+2.1k USD/day if left overnight.

taylor: if root cause is driver, this needs infra-hw rollback/backport patch. also we should avoid leaving increased warm-pool sizes long-term. can someone file a short postmortem and tag dedicated-capacity owners so they can decide on cost vs SLA for eu-west1c?

morgan: will open an incident note and assign OWNER: elena + taylor. tagging @dedicated-capacity for visibility. thanks all :thumbsup:

elena: creating HW ticket and starting a small canary rollback to 534.x on one rack. will report back.

morgan: noted. I'll keep monitoring and post updates in this thread.
